t: Sixty per centum of the expenditures for the District Court of the United States for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title and 30 per centum of the expenditures for the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title shall be reimbursed to the United States from any funds in the Treasury to the credit of the District of Columbia.

fable.w: This is a fiscal provision requiring that a share of federal court expenditures be reimbursed from District of Columbia funds in the Treasury. The tempting reading is that the mention of the District of Columbia, a non-federal local government, signals outside involvement. That fails because the District is only a source of funds: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue attached to any federal decision.
fable.s: shall be reimbursed to the United States from any funds in the Treasury to the credit of the District of Columbia

qwen_block.w: This section describes a financial reimbursement mechanism between the federal government and the District of Columbia. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory process with outside parties before a decision is made. The District of Columbia is a local government entity, but the text only mandates a transfer of funds, not participation in decision-making.
qwen_block.s: Sixty per centum of the expenditures for the District Court of the United States for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title and 30 per centum of the expenditures for the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title shall be reimbursed to the United States from any funds in the Treasury to the credit of the District of Columbia.

opus.w: This section only sets out how the District of Columbia's Treasury funds will pay back part of the expenditures for two federal courts. The District of Columbia is named, but only as a source of money. It is not consulted and takes no part in any federal decision, so nothing outside the federal government is brought into a decision. Like Example 1, this is a funding provision, not participation.
opus.s: shall be reimbursed to the United States from any funds in the Treasury to the credit of the District of Columbia
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through:** One could be tempted to answer "Yes" because the District of Columbia, a non-federal government, is named. But it only appears as the source of funds that pay the United States back for court costs. No outside party is consulted, coordinated with, or given a say in any federal decision. There is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. This is a funding provision, like Example 1.

2. **Label:**

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates a financial reimbursement from the District of Columbia to the federal government. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or input from the District of Columbia or any other outside party regarding a federal decision. The definition of participation requires that the government consult or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision, which is not happening here; this is simply a transfer of funds.
qwen_chat.s: Sixty per centum of the expenditures for the District Court of the United States for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title and 30 per centum of the expenditures for the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia from all appropriations under this title shall be reimbursed to the United States from any funds in the Treasury to the credit of the District of Columbia.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the District of Columbia is a local government entity, any financial interaction involving it constitutes "coordination" or "participation." However, this section merely mandates a reimbursement of funds from the District's treasury to the federal treasury. It does not require the District to consult with the federal government, provide input, or participate in a decision-making process before the reimbursement occurs. It is a fiscal mandate, not a participatory process.
